Italy.text: Its first World Heritage Site, the Rock Drawings in Valcamonica, was listed in 1979.
Italy.evidence: The first site in Italy, the Rock Drawings in Valcamonica, was listed at the 3rd Session of the World Heritage Committee, held in Cairo and Luxor, Egypt, in 1979.

China.text: Its first six sites were listed in 1987; its newest, in 2026, are the Jingdezhen porcelain sites.
China.evidence: The first sites in China were added to the list in 1987 when six sites were inscribed. The most recent additions took place in 2026 when the Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites were listed.

France.text: The Beaches of the D-Day Landings became one of its World Heritage Sites in 2026.
France.evidence: The first five sites in France were added to the list in 1979 while the most recent, the Beaches of the D-Day Landings and the Royal Capetian Fortresses of Languedoc, were added in 2026.

Germany.text: West and East Germany joined the convention separately; Aachen Cathedral was listed first, in 1978.
Germany.evidence: As Germany was divided following World War II, West and East Germany ratified the convention separately, the former on 23 August 1976 and the latter on 12 December 1988. The first site listed was the Aachen Cathedral in 1978.

Spain.text: Its first sites were listed in 1984, at a UNESCO session held in Buenos Aires.
Spain.evidence: Sites in Spain were first inscribed on the list at the 8th Session of the World Heritage Committee, held in Buenos Aires, Argentina in 1984.

India.text: The Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and the Ajanta and Ellora Caves were its first sites, listed in 1983.
India.evidence: The first sites to be listed were the Ajanta Caves, Ellora Caves, Agra Fort, and Taj Mahal, all of which were inscribed in the 1983 session of the World Heritage Committee.

Mexico.text: Its newest site, listed in 2025, is the Wixárika route through sacred sites to Wirikuta.
Mexico.evidence: The most recent inscription was the Wixárika Route through Sacred Sites to Wirikuta, listed in 2025.

United Kingdom.text: Stonehenge and the Giant's Causeway were among its first sites, listed in 1986.
United Kingdom.evidence: The first sites in the UK to be inscribed on the World Heritage List were Giant's Causeway and Causeway Coast; Durham Castle and Cathedral; Ironbridge Gorge; Studley Royal Park including the Ruins of Fountains Abbey; Stonehenge, Avebury and Associated Sites; and the Castles and Town Walls of King Edward in Gwynedd in 1986.

Russia.text: Its first five sites were listed in 1990, while it was still part of the Soviet Union.
Russia.evidence: The first five sites in the Soviet Union were inscribed to the list at the 14th session of the UNESCO World Heritage Committee, held in Banff, Alberta, Canada, in December 1990.

Iran.text: Persepolis and Isfahan's great square were among its first three sites, listed in 1979.
Iran.evidence: The first three sites in Iran, Meidan Naghshe Jahan, Isfahan, Persepolis and Tchogha Zanbil, were inscribed on the list at the Third Session of the World Heritage Committee, held in Cairo and Luxor, Egypt in 1979.
